claim_being_audited: That certifying the model for launch is compliant and evidentially supported because aggregate readiness passed, launch rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and public AI-governance guidance permits measured deployment with documented limitations and monitoring despite the unresolved legal-intake-triage gap.
decision_criteria: Use 'compliant' only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold for certification.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case.
Product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when the affected segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending.
Material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Aggregate readiness and rehearsal results are supporting context, not substitutes for satisfying the disclosure policy predicate.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the legal intake triage gap must be disclosed for the named pilot commitments.
Approved risk-acceptance record, if any, covering this specific named launch use case before launch.
Launch materials or model-card disclosure showing the limitation was actually disclosed to the affected commitments.
Evidence that the named pilot commitments are not contractual customer segments or named launch use cases under policy, if that is the intended rebuttal.
specific_concerns: The admissible record shows a 1.2-point miss in the legal intake triage segment, and that segment is named in two law-firm pilot commitments.
Policy text says a weakness is material when it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case; product's 'non-core' framing does not resolve that predicate.
The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, and no approved risk acceptance is in evidence.
Public model-card and NIST-style governance guidance support documentation and monitoring practices, but they do not by themselves authorize certification under the internal disclosure policy.
unsupported_claims: The packet overreaches by treating aggregate readiness and clean rehearsal as sufficient support for certification despite an unresolved materiality/disclosure predicate.
Any implication that public governance guidance alone makes this launch compliant is unsupported by the admissible record.
There is no admissible evidence that the disclosure obligation has been satisfied, waived, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
